text:
alex: FYI — escalating ACME on-prem private deployment. They've reported intermittent 502s and long tails (524) when calling our hosted endpoint through a corporate proxy in their air-gapped site. Root says proxy uses NTLM + TLS inspect.

maria: Can you paste the minimal repro/logs and the curl you ran? Also confirm whether they run in 'no-internet' mode (eg no external DNS/OCSP).

customer-ops: pasted logs below. we tried from a test container:
```bash
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
Result: `* Proxy replied 407` then after retry `* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, description = unknown CA` and curl eventually times out. `--insecure` makes the request succeed (but we can't do that in prod).

alex: that matches TLS intercept/mitm. Most likely the proxy is re-signing certs with a corporate CA not trusted by the container. Two things to confirm: 1) is the proxy doing SNI passthrough or terminate+re-sign, 2) does the container trust the corp CA bundle?

ingrid: quick repro steps to validate CA vs auth: from the same host run:
```bash
# check proxy auth flow
curl -v --proxy-user "CORP\\user:password" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health || true
# dump cert chain seen by curl
openssl s_client -showcerts -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -connect proxy.corp:443 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/BEGIN CERT/,/END CERT/p'
```
Note: openssl against proxy gives the proxy's cert if it terminates TLS. If proxy is CONNECTing, you need to `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.internal:443` from a host with direct egress or use `openssl s_client -proxy proxy.corp:8080 -connect api.redwood-inference.internal:443` (some builds support `-proxy`).

ben: also confirm REDWOOD side egress allowlist/IP restrictions. If their proxy NATs many internal hosts through a small set of egress IPs, our IP allowlist may be blocking or rate-limiting them causing 502s and long tails.

customer-ops: we do NAT through three egress IPs (list provided in DM). We do have corporate CA but because it's air-gapped we can't attach it here. We validated that `curl --insecure` works and responses are normal; without `--insecure` we see `unknown ca`. Latency is higher when proxy does TLS inspect (adds ~200ms) and occasionally we see 524 after ~30s.

maria: mitigation options: 1) add corporate CA to container/system trust stores (recommended), 2) configure proxy for SNI passthrough for our hostnames so TLS is end-to-end, or 3) if unavoidable, set up a private peering/outbound gateway so traffic doesn't traverse TLS-inspecting proxy.

alex: short-term repro ask for ops: can you run `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --proxy-user 'CORP\\user:REDACTED' https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health` and paste the `* Server certificate` chain? Also need `traceroute -T -p 443 api.redwood-inference.internal` and a small tcpdump of the SYN/ACKs to confirm retries.

customer-ops: running now, will paste shortly.

ops-bot: Reminder: support escalation ticket #SE-4771 created and linked to this thread.

ingrid: one more subtle thing — if the proxy rewrites Host/SNI or terminates and re-signs, OCSP/OCSP stapling may fail and some clients see intermittent handshake failures. Check whether the proxy performs OCSP caching or strips stapled responses.

ben: assigned to infra-oncall to validate egress allowlist and to product-support for private deployment config. Suggest temporary canary: allowlist their NAT IPs for 24h and ask them to test without proxy in a small subnet to confirm.

alex: next steps and timeline: customer to provide cert chain + tcpdump (ETA 2h). Infra will validate allowlist and we will test SNI passthrough config in lab (ETA 4h). If they can't add corp CA to trust stores, we have a plan B: route their private control plane through a dedicated egress that bypasses TLS-inspect proxies.

maria: thanks all — adding :thumbsup: and pinging @ingrid for cert analysis once logs arrive.

customer-ops: uploaded redacted cert PEMs to the ticket and captured tcpdump. confirmed behavior reproducible from 3 different hosts behind same proxy.

alex: great — keeping this thread as the single source. I'll update SE-4771 with progress. :white_check_mark:
